A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GESPI framework, authors, applications, and Appendices A–J. The text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on image classification, protein structure prediction, outlier detection, LLM comparisons, and CLIP interpretability, plus simulations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices C and J, including numerical coverage and prediction-set-size results in Tables S3–S4.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 newly suggests an optional goodness-of-fit screening step comparing synthetic and real empirical risks, with a real-only fallback at level α. This is a limited proposed procedural addition; the aggregation rules in Eqs. (1)–(6) and the evaluated GESPI construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet/FLUX classification and interpretability studies, CASP-14/MSA protein inference, Shuttle/Credit Card/KDDCup99 outlier detection, AIME25/OlympiadBench LLM comparisons, and binomial simulations. No evaluated dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: OnlyReal, Guardrail, OnlySynth, Oracle in outlier detection, SPI in Figure S10, and Synth+Real in Appendix J. The newly cited related methods are not added to the evaluations.

E3.justification: The reported splits, sample sizes, metrics, model configurations, and testing procedures are retained. For example, image classification still uses 15 real, 1,000 synthetic, and 500 test images per class. The new ε-selection advice does not revise the experimental settings.

E4.justification: The existing sensitivity studies of ε, α, sample sizes, and synthetic-data quality, coverage-matched comparisons, trimming analyses, and protein/CLIP case studies are retained. The proposed screening step receives no new ablation or robustness evaluation.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same replication and uncertainty practices, including 100 image-classification runs, 10 protein trials, the nested 50-by-50 LLM evaluation, and standard errors in Tables S3–S4. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting change is evident.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Magpie coverage remains 95.8% for GESPI versus 100% for OnlyReal in Table S3, with prediction-set sizes 4.0 versus 30 in Table S4.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Conditions 3.2 and F.1, theoretical guarantees, impossibility result, and proofs in Appendices D–I retain their substance. The added practical guidance supplies no new formal assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow applicability from wrapping around 'any' statistical inference procedure to 'a broad class' of procedures. The central claims about distribution-free guarantees, adaptation to synthetic-data quality, and utility are otherwise retained.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 expands the existing risk–utility discussion into practical advice connecting ε to application-specific risk tolerance and beliefs about synthetic-data quality. It also interprets significant empirical-risk differences as grounds to avoid synthetic data. Existing result interpretations and Section 5 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds explicit tuning heuristics such as ε = 0.2α or 0.5α without changing documented experiments. It also omits the direct FLUX.1-dev model URL previously supplied in the references. The experiment code link and Appendix B implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds Ji et al. (2025) to prediction-powered inference discussion and contrasts Byun et al. (2025)'s moment-based approach and unlabeled-corpus assumption with GESPI. The broader positioning is retained; most other reference changes concern metadata or editions of existing works.

P1.justification: The title changes to 'General Synthetic-Powered Inference.' v3 adds practical ε guidance, a brief Impact Statement, and conference/correspondence information, with reference-style updates. Most prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, extensively resizing and repositioning figures, equations, and captions. Table 1 is transposed, and Figure 5's legend moves into a horizontal arrangement above the plots. Appendix material is also reflowed without adding or removing scientific displays.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision by narrowing the overbroad applicability claim and adds useful practical guidance and related-work context. The evidence and proofs remain unchanged, and the optional screening proposal is unevaluated, so the gains are limited. Omitting the direct FLUX model link is a small reproducibility drawback, outweighed by the clearer scope and guidance.
